questions.q: In Islamic architecture, what is the term for the niche in the wall of a mosque that indicates the direction of Mecca?
questions.n: The mihrab is a semi-circular niche in the wall of a mosque that indicates the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca.

questions.q: What is the name of the tall, slender tower from which the faithful are called to prayer?
questions.n: Minarets serve as visual focal points and functional towers for the adhan (call to prayer).

questions.q: Which world-famous funerary monument in Agra, India, was built by Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal?
questions.n: Constructed of white marble, it is considered the pinnacle of Mughal architecture and a symbol of eternal love.

questions.q: What is the decorative 'honeycomb' or 'stalactite' vaulting often found in Islamic domes and niches?
questions.n: Muqarnas are three-dimensional decorative elements that transition between flat surfaces and curved domes or arches.

questions.q: What is the 'direction of prayer' towards the Kaaba in Mecca called?
questions.n: Qibla is the fixed direction of the Kaaba, which all Muslims face during their daily prayers.

questions.q: Which Art Nouveau architect is famous for the organic, 'melting' forms of the Casa Batlló and the Sagrada Familia?
questions.n: Gaudí’s work in Barcelona is unique for its integration of crafts like ceramics, stained glass, and wrought iron into naturalistic forms.

questions.q: What is the name of the 'whiplash' curve motif commonly seen in Art Nouveau ironwork and graphics?
questions.n: The whiplash curve or 'coup de fouet' is a signature of Art Nouveau, inspired by the stems of lilies and other plants.

questions.q: The Chrysler Building in New York, with its sunburst top and stainless steel ornaments, is a prime example of which style?
questions.n: Art Deco celebrated the Machine Age through luxury materials, bold colors, and streamlined, symmetrical shapes.

questions.q: Which French architect designed the Metro Station Entrances in Paris, icons of the Art Nouveau movement?
questions.n: Guimard's cast-iron and glass entrances brought the organic lines of Art Nouveau into the everyday urban landscape of Paris.

questions.q: Art Deco is often characterized by what type of geometry (as opposed to the organic lines of Art Nouveau)?
questions.n: Art Deco focused on the beauty of the machine, using bold vertical lines and repetitive geometric patterns.

questions.q: Who is the architect who famously coined the phrase 'Less is More'?
questions.n: Mies van der Rohe's work was defined by extreme simplicity and the 'skin and bones' architecture of steel and glass.

questions.q: Which building in New York, designed by Mies van der Rohe and Philip Johnson, set the standard for the modern glass-and-bronze skyscraper?
questions.n: Completed in 1958, its use of bronze and its functionalist elegance defined corporate architecture for decades.

questions.q: In Le Corbusier's 'Five Points of New Architecture,' which point refers to the columns that lift the building off the ground?
questions.n: Pilotis are reinforced concrete columns that raise the building, allowing the ground space to flow underneath.

questions.q: Which building is considered Le Corbusier's masterpiece of the International Style, located in Poissy, France?
questions.n: The Villa Savoye perfectly embodies the Five Points of Architecture and the concept of the house as a 'machine for living'.

questions.q: What is the term for the non-structural outer skin of a building, typical of Modernist high-rises?
questions.n: A curtain wall is an exterior cladding system that is attached to the building structure but does not carry any structural loads.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the National Museum of Fine Arts (formerly the Legislative Building)?
questions.n: Arellano was a master of the Neoclassical style in the Philippines, also designing the Post Office Building.

questions.q: Which architect designed the GSIS Building in Pasay and the Sulo Hotel?
questions.n: Ilustre was a government architect known for his distinctive modern approach to state buildings.

questions.q: Which firm is the primary Architect of Record for many SM projects, including the SM Mall of Asia complex?
questions.n: Founded by Albert Yu, ASYA Design has been instrumental in the rapid expansion of the SM mall and residential portfolio.

questions.q: Who is the primary architect (or design consultant) behind the SM Aura Premier and the Discovery Primea?
questions.n: Kenzo Tange Associates served as the design consultant for these high-end developments.

questions.q: Which National Artist designed the 1953 Exposition 'Philippines International Fair' and the Rizal Memorial Stadium?
questions.n: Nakpil was a dominant force in mid-century Philippine architecture, blending modern and Art Deco influences.

questions.q: In a Bahay na Bato, what is the name of the 'grand staircase' that leads from the lower floor to the living quarters?
questions.n: The escalera was a significant architectural feature, often made of fine hardwood to showcase the family's wealth.

questions.q: What is the name of the spacious 'living room' used for receiving important guests and for social gatherings?
questions.n: The antesala is the most public area of the upper floor, used for social events and receiving visitors.

questions.q: What is the dining room called in a Bahay na Bato?
questions.n: The comedor was often located near the cocina and the azotea for convenience.

questions.q: In a Bahay na Bato, where were water jars (tapayan) traditionally kept for drinking and household use?
questions.n: The azotea served as a multi-purpose outdoor space where water jars were often stored for easy access from the kitchen.

questions.q: What is the name of the 'sleeping room' or private quarters in a Bahay na Bato?
questions.n: These were the private family areas, usually located away from the public antesala.
